blocks.content: 85, 22607 Hamburg, Germany 5Regionales Rechenzentrum, Universität Hamburg, 20146 Hamburg, Germany (Received 4 February 2025; accepted 29 April 2025; published 20 May 2025) The Compton amplitude subtraction function is an essential component in work concerning both the proton radius puzzle and the proton-neutron mass difference.
Here, we use the Feynman-Hellmann method to determine this subtraction function directly from lattice QCD.

The Compton amplitude subtraction function, S1ðQ2Þ, is a critical component in the theoretical determination of the proton-neutron mass difference, and a necessary quantity for the calculation of the proton charge radius.
In this context, a first-principles lattice QCD evaluation of the Compton amplitude subtraction function is crucial.
Recently a lattice calculation of the subtraction function was performed using four-point correlation functions [24], following on from earlier work [25,26].

In this paper, we determine the Compton amplitude subtraction function over the range 1 ≲Q2 ≲16 GeV2 at the standard subtraction point using the Feynman- Hellmann technique, which has previously been used to determine the structure function moments for the forward [28–30] and off-forward [31,32] Compton amplitudes.
V we remove the leading order discretization artifacts and, in doing so, present the Compton amplitude subtraction function, and compare it with the continuum OPE expectation.

blocks.title: I. INTRODUCTION
blocks.content:
The Compton amplitude subtraction function, S1ðQ2Þ, is
a critical component in the theoretical determination of the
proton-neutron mass difference, and a necessary quantity
for the calculation of the proton charge radius. However,
the subtraction function is not directly measurable from
experiment, and as such contributes significant theoretical
and statistical uncertainties to these quantities. In this
context, a first-principles determination of the subtraction
function could play a vital role in clarifying our under-
standing of hadron structure.

blocks.title: III. FEYNMAN-HELLMANN METHOD
blocks.content:

as the Compton amplitude [28–32].

blocks.title: IV. DISCRETIZATION ARTIFACTS
blocks.content:
As with all lattice calculations, it is necessary to take into
account, and correct for, discretization artifacts present in
the results. The subtraction function, more so than other
quantities, suffers from such artifacts to a large degree. This
is analogous to short-distance artifacts studied in the case of
the hadronic vacuum polarization [47,48].
